title: Spiced split pea pot with marrow and broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or ordinary cupboard staple, and vegetable stock is explicitly allowed.

supermarket.reason: Yellow split peas, marrow, broccoli and the spices are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded pan, a knife and a wooden spoon, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas in 1.2 litres of stock, simmered for an hour in total with a whole marrow and broccoli, gives a well-spiced pot for four with sensible liquid and timings.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers chopping onions, garlic and tomatoes, peeling and seeding the marrow, cutting florets and the 8-minute soften, and the simmer steps of 40, 15 and 5 minutes add up to the 60 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the lemon and fresh coriander, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A whole marrow in chunks is a main part of the pot and fits mid-August, when marrows are plentiful.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pulses with plenty of vegetables make a filling, wholesome lunch a family would happily eat again.
